candidates.attacker_control: The `sector_identifier_uri` field of the JSON client-registration request (POST /realms/{realm}/clients-registrations/openid-connect or /default, create or update) is fully attacker-chosen, as is the host/path/query of the URL. In the admin path the same value comes from client/mapper configuration set by a manage-clients caller. The only pre-fetch checks are `new URI(value)` succeeding and having non-null scheme and host (PairwiseSubMapperValidator lines 70-82); `http://`, `https://`, IP literals, localhost and metadata-style hosts all pass.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Fetching the sector identifier URI is required by the OIDC pairwise-subject/Dynamic Client Registration specification, so the request itself is intended behavior; however the snapshot adds no destination constraints, no HTTPS requirement, and no private-address blocking, leaving an SSRF primitive. The response body is parsed into a list of strings and never echoed to the client, so exfiltration is limited (semi-blind). Anonymous dynamic client registration is effectively blocked by the default Trusted Hosts policy (empty trusted-hosts with host/client-URI match flags true), so a deployment must have issued an Initial Access Token or configured trusted hosts; the admin-initiated variant requires manage-clients. The `secure-client-uris` client-policy executor exists in this snapshot but does not cover sector_identifier_uri and only applies when a client profile is bound.
candidates.impact: Server-originated requests to arbitrary hosts/ports from the Keycloak server (SSRF): probing/consuming internal-only HTTP services, hitting cloud metadata endpoints with GET, bypassing network ACLs for GET-capable endpoints, and resource-exhaustion by pointing at large/slow responses. Because the fetched JSON is only used to compare redirect-URI values and is not returned, the primary impact is request forgery plus a validation-error oracle rather than direct response disclosure.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) A way to create or update a client: dynamic client registration enabled with a valid Initial Access Token (or anonymous registration permitted by the realm's client-registration policies / trusted hosts), or an admin with manage-clients; (2) the URI must contain a scheme and host; (3) the target URL must be reachable from the Keycloak server. The fetch is blind/semi-blind: only success/JSON-parse/validation error outcomes are observable.
candidates.root_cause: Client metadata field sector_identifier_uri is parsed and validated only for URI syntactics (scheme/host must be present) and is then fetched server-side before any destination restriction: PairwiseSubMapperValidator.getSectorRedirects() calls session.getProvider(HttpClientProvider.class).get(sectorIdentifierUri) and parses the response as JSON. There is no allow-list of hosts, no HTTPS-only enforcement (http:// is accepted), and no blocking of loopback/private/link-local addresses; the shared client (DefaultHttpClientFactory) performs a plain HttpGet(uri). The same request also triggers the fetch through the non-OIDC validation path when a client has a pairwise mapper with a sector identifier configured.
candidates.title: SSRF via unvalidated sector_identifier_uri during OIDC client registration/validation
candidates.trace: OIDCClientRegistrationProvider.createOIDC() line 95 -> validateClient(clientModel, clientOIDC, true) -> AbstractClientRegistrationProvider.validateClient() lines 198-203 -> ValidationUtil.validateClient() picks ClientValidationContext.OIDCContext (lines 31-42) -> DefaultClientValidationProvider.validate(OIDCContext) lines 143-151 -> validatePairwiseInOIDCClient() lines 238-248 (fires when subject_type=pairwise OR sector_identifier_uri is non-empty) -> validatePairwise() lines 250-260 -> PairwiseSubMapperValidator.validate(session, rootUrl, redirectUris, sectorIdentifierUri) lines 39-46 -> validateSectorIdentifierUri(session, ...) lines 84-90 -> getSectorRedirects() line 95 -> HttpClientProvider.get(sectorIdentifierUri) -> DefaultHttpClientFactory.get() line 110-112 -> HttpGet(uri)/httpClient.execute(). Update path: OIDCClientRegistrationProvider lines 126-137; admin path: ClientsResource ~line 202 / ClientResource ~line 150 -> ClientModel validation -> validatePairwiseInClientModel lines 229-236 -> same fetch.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or request was performed. It was not verified that the shared HttpClient/ProxyMappings configuration cannot block loopback/link-local targets, nor whether specific deployments issue Initial Access Tokens; the exact upstream fix commit/CVE for this behavior was not inspected. The P1 index is syntactic only and was used solely for navigation.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot only: 5,889 model-visible files (4,704 Java); P1 relation index covers 5,798 files with 91 source files missing from the index (syntactic navigation only — no control/data flow, no reachability). Focused on server-side Java: services (client registration, OIDC/SAML protocol endpoints, account/admin REST, authentication/authenticators, client policies, validation, UMA protection API, theme/resource loading), server-spi(-private), core, saml-core, federation/ldap, quarkus/runtime and adapters. Searched for injection sinks (SQL/JPQL/native query concatenation, OS command, LDAP, XPath), SSRF/HTTP fetch sinks, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, XXE/StAX configuration, HTML string building, CSRF, redirect-URI handling, and authorization-check patterns. Non-Java assets filtered out of the snapshot (.ftl, .css, .adoc) could not be inspected; testsuite, distribution, operator and examples were sampled rather than exhaustively reviewed.
limitations: Review is static only: no code execution, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run; nothing is runtime-confirmed.
The P1 index is a syntactic/navigation index (no data-flow or semantic resolution) and omitted 91 files / 94 files; absence from the index is not evidence of safety.
FreeMarker templates (.ftl), CSS and docs (.adoc) are excluded from the visible snapshot, so template-level XSS/rendering issues could not be verified.
Deployment-specific configuration (anonymous dynamic client registration, Initial Access Tokens, X.509 CRL/OCSP options, proxy mappings, client policies) could not be confirmed from the source alone.
Because only one candidate may be submitted, other plausible flows (noted in rejected leads) were not exhaustively traced to a concrete exploit path.

rejected_leads.lead: X.509 CRL-distribution-point/OCSP server-side fetch (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/x509/CertificateValidator.java lines 310-333, 743-763): revocation check runs before trust validation and fetches the certificate's CRL DP via HTTP/LDAP.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires the X.509 authenticator configured with CRL checking/CRL-DP or OCSP enabled, and the reachability of the revocation path for an untrusted certificate was not fully verified from source; config-gated and lower likelihood of being the benchmark case.

rejected_leads.lead: request_uris fetch: client-registered request_uris are fetched by the auth/PAR/CIBA endpoints (AuthorizationEndpointRequestParserProcessor.java lines 95-104, ParEndpointRequestParserProcessor.java lines 86-95; BackchannelAuthenticationEndpointRequestParserProcessor.java lines 66-76).
rejected_leads.reason: Same root-cause family (client-controlled URL fetched server-side) but requires the value to be pre-registered on a client and is triggered at authorization time; kept as an alternative rather than a separate candidate to avoid splitting one root cause.

rejected_leads.lead: TrustedHostClientRegistrationPolicy domain match uses host.endsWith(trustedDomain) (lines 173, 234), so a trusted domain 'example.com' also matches 'evilexample.com'.
rejected_leads.reason: Real policy-weakening pattern, but requires dynamic client registration plus wildcard trusted-domain configuration and successful end-to-end exploitation was not verified against source; impact and ground-truth match are weaker than the SSRF candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: SAML artifact/logout POST form builds ACTION attribute from an unescaped ACS/artifact URL (saml-core BaseSAML2BindingBuilder.buildHtmlForm line 342; SamlProtocol.artifactPost line 980 with redirectUri from client attributes set without URI validation in SamlService lines 431-433).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a crafted SAML client attribute (manage-clients/admin or client-description import) and artifact binding; main SAML response path uses the (excluded) saml-post-form.ftl template, so no clear unauthenticated exploit path was established.

rejected_leads.lead: OIDCRedirectUriBuilder form_post ACTION and RedirectUtils wildcard prefix matching look potentially unsafe.
rejected_leads.reason: redirect URIs are parsed via URI.create()/normalize() before use (quotes and control characters are rejected) and wildcard matching is standard suffix-wildcard behavior; no concrete exploit path was identified.

summary: Keycloak master snapshot (999-SNAPSHOT, ~late-2022; newest JPA changelog is 20.0.0 and no 2023-dated files). After broad review of server-side Java with emphasis on attacker-controlled input reaching sensitive sinks, the single strongest source-verified lead is a server-side request forgery: the client-supplied OIDC `sector_identifier_uri` is fetched by the Keycloak server via the shared HTTP client during client registration/update validation, with no allow-list, no HTTPS requirement, and no private/link-local address restriction. The fetch is triggered straight from the registration/update request body, so a caller allowed to register a client (dynamic client registration with an initial access token, or a realm admin with manage-clients) can make the server issue HTTP GETs to arbitrary internal URLs. Other plausible issues are listed as rejected leads because they are config-gated, lower impact, or less clearly exploitable. No finding was runtime-confirmed.
